metadata.title: Dashboard Page with Navigation and Quick Actions

story.iWant: to see a dashboard with overview of workload and quick actions
story.soThat: I can quickly navigate to common tasks

tasks.task: Create layout structure with Header and Sidebar (AC: #2, #3, #4)
Implement navigation menu with role-based visibility (AC: #3, #5)
Implement loading states with skeleton loaders (AC: #10)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Dashboard page created at route /dashboard (protected route, requires auth)
Header section displays app logo/title, user greeting, user profile dropdown, time-of-day greeting
Sidebar navigation with menu items (Dashboard, Customers, Policies, Audit Log, Reports, Admin) with role-based visibility
Sidebar collapses on mobile devices (hamburger menu)
Active menu item highlighted based on current route
Main content area displays quick actions: "New Customer", "New Policy", search inputs
Optional metrics dashboard with customer/policy counts and recent activity feed
Responsive design: sidebar collapses on mobile, main content full width
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+K opens search modal (search customers globally)
Loading state while fetching metrics (skeleton loaders)

doc.title: Epic Breakdown - EPIC 3: React Frontend - Authentication & Core UI
doc.section: Story 3.3: Dashboard Page with Navigation and Quick Actions
doc.snippet: Defines dashboard layout with header, sidebar, role-based navigation, quick action buttons, optional metrics, and keyboard shortcuts for improved UX.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Documents main application layout patterns, role-based navigation implementation, responsive design breakpoints, and accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA).

doc.title: Data Models
doc.snippet: Defines User type with roles array, role types (customer_service_agent, compliance_officer, admin), and how roles determine menu visibility and feature access.

doc.title: Story 3.2: Login Page and Zitadel OIDC Authentication
doc.snippet: Story 3.2 extracts user roles from JWT claims. Story 3.3 uses these roles to filter menu items and control feature access via role-based visibility.

artifact.reason: Story 3.1 establishes project structure, React Router setup, MUI configuration. Story 3.3 uses Layout wrapper for all protected routes.
Story 3.2 provides AuthContext with user info and roles. Story 3.3 uses useAuth() hook to get user roles for menu filtering and display user greeting.

constraint.rule: Menu items must be filtered based on user roles from JWT. Roles: [] (all users), ['compliance_officer', 'admin'] (specific roles), ['admin'] (admin only).
Layout component (Header + Sidebar + Outlet) must wrap all protected routes. Unprotected routes like /login should NOT use Layout.
Sidebar collapses to hamburger menu on mobile (MUI breakpoint: md). Use MUI breakpoints system (xs, sm, md, lg, xl).
Compare useLocation().pathname with menu item paths. Highlight exact matches. Support nested routes.
Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K on Mac) opens search modal for searching customers globally. Implement keyboard event listener at root level.

interface.name: Layout Component
interface.signature: Layout component that wraps Header, Sidebar, and Outlet for protected routes
interface.description: Root layout component for authenticated users. Combines Header (top nav with user menu) and Sidebar (left navigation) with main content area.

interface.name: useAuth Hook
interface.signature: const {user, isAuthenticated, logout} = useAuth() - provides user context with roles
interface.description: Custom hook providing authenticated user information including roles. Used by Sidebar to filter menu items and Header to display user greeting.

interface.name: Menu Configuration
interface.signature: MenuItem[] with {label, icon, path, roles?} - configurable menu items with role filters
interface.description: Centralized menu configuration defining available navigation items, their icons, routes, and required roles for visibility.

interface.name: useLocation Hook
interface.signature: const location = useLocation() - provides current route pathname for active menu highlighting
interface.description: React Router hook for getting current pathname to determine which menu item should be highlighted as active.

tests.standards: Unit tests use Jest + React Testing Library. Test layout rendering, role-based menu filtering, responsive behavior, and keyboard shortcuts. Manual testing required for mobile layouts.

locations.location: src/components/__tests__/Sidebar.test.tsx - Sidebar navigation tests with role-based filtering
src/components/__tests__/Header.test.tsx - Header and user menu tests

ideas.idea: Verify dashboard page renders with Header showing app logo, user greeting, and time-of-day message
Verify user profile dropdown menu appears, contains Profile/Settings/Logout options
Verify Sidebar displays all menu items, filters hidden items based on user roles
Verify Sidebar collapses to hamburger on mobile (DevTools responsive mode, md breakpoint)
Verify current menu item highlighted when navigating to its route
Verify quick action buttons navigate to correct routes (/customers/create, /policies/create, etc.)
Verify metrics dashboard loads customer/policy counts and displays recent activity
Verify Ctrl+K opens search modal (test with keyboard listener)
Verify skeleton loaders appear while fetching metrics data
Verify logout clears session and redirects to /login
